items.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Śiva alone, possessing spanda, self-established, makes the inner face taste; this hero, lord of the Kula, is victorious. Kṣemarāja's commentary: whose greatness is unmeasured, who measures the world from earth to Sadāśiva in the heart, who displays creation-dissolution plays — he alone, of non-dual nature, endowed with his own autonomy-power, established in his own nature, like an ocean unmoved by world-waves, shines supreme. Recognition (pratyabhijñā) is tasting this spanda in one's own inner face.

paragraphs.text: One winner, ever: Shiva. Self-throbbing, self-standing, tasting everything from the inside out. No committee, no contest.

He is the lord of the entire Kula — the whole family of everything that is. Unmeasured himself, he measures the world end to end inside his own heart, runs creation and destruction like plays, and does not move while the world waves crash. Non-dual, self-powered, supreme.
And the punchline is you: recognition means tasting that exact same throb in your own inward face. That is it. That is the whole thing.
